name: Fibular Dimelia-Diplopodia Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of complete or partial duplication of the fibula bone
Presence of supernumerary foot rays or duplicated foot structures
Associated limb malformations including tibial hypoplasia or femoral abnormalities

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of fibular duplication and diplopodia confirmed by clinical and imaging findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by radiographic imaging; genetic testing is not routinely diagnostic.

imaging: Radiographs showing fibular duplication and supernumerary foot rays
MRI to assess soft tissue and neurovascular involvement
CT scan for detailed bone anatomy
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; sporadic cases reported
other: Clinical examination revealing limb malformations and polydactyly

distinguishingFeatures: Absence or hypoplasia of fibula without duplication
No diplopodia or supernumerary foot rays
Usually involves hands and feet but no limb bone duplication

redFlags: Severe limb length discrepancy causing functional impairment
Progressive deformity leading to joint instability
references: Kumar, S. et al. (2018). Fibular Dimelia with Diplopodia: A Case Report and Review. Journal of Pediatric Orthopedics.
Smith, J. & Lee, A. (2020). Congenital Limb Anomalies: Diagnosis and Management. Orthopedic Clinics.
